title: Friday night dinner ride
summary: A Friday evening ride out for dinner with his wife: a rainbow running through a cloud over the ridge, no bike lights, and a sunset on the way home.

post.title: Friday night dinner ride
post.body:
Friday night, my wife and I decided dinner was worth riding to. Helmets on, across the main road and up a back way that's more dirt than road, a bit bumpy and a lot more fun than driving.

A few minutes in I stopped for the sky. Over the ridge there was a cloud with a rainbow running through it, pink, green and violet like oil on water.

Ordering went fine. Then we realized neither of us had brought a bike light, and the sun was already heading behind the Sierra. Dinner to go, and home the long way on the best-lit roads we know.

The sky made up for it on the way back: a long pink streak over the mountains and the sagebrush going dark below it.

What I learned: pack the lights, even for a ride to dinner.

episode.title: Pack the lights
episode.script:
It's a Friday evening in early October, a little after six. Christian and his wife decide that dinner tonight will be reached by bike.

Helmets on. Out across the main road, then up a back way that is more dirt than road. Bumpy. A little off-road for two people heading out for dinner. Nobody minds.

***

A few minutes in, Christian looks up and stops.

Over the dark ridge of the mountains there's a cloud doing something clouds rarely do. Pale gold at the edges, and through the middle, a smear of every colour. Pink, green, violet, all running together like oil on water. A rainbow, folded into a cloud.

He takes three pictures. Then they ride on.

***

Dinner is the easy part. The ordering goes fine. And that's when they notice what they don't have.

Lights.

The sun is already on its way down behind the Sierra. Neither of them has brought a bike light. So the plan changes. Dinner to go. And a ride home on the best-lit roads they know, rather than the bumpy way they came.

***

On the way back, the sky puts on a second show. The sagebrush goes dark and quiet. Behind the mountains the light turns cream, then pink, a long streak of it stretched across the sky, glowing at the edges of the ridge.

Christian stops once more for that.

***

They get home safe, in the last of the light. And a few minutes later they're sitting down to a hot dinner, earned the long way round.

Lesson noted, again. Pack the lights. Even for dinner.
